title: Expected Mac Reports FileVault Not Enabled
exclusions: Compares active expected Macs with normalized Apple MDM SecurityInfo or declarative FileVault-status snapshots. It reports no observation in 48 hours, stale status older than 24 hours, or explicit `filevault_enabled=false`. These windows and local fields are deployment policy. FileVault-on status does not prove a personal recovery key is escrowed/current, every authorized user has a secure token, the startup volume finished conversion, the Mac is physically secure, or any regulation is satisfied. Recovery-key material must never be indexed.
evidence: Retain the `expected_macos_filevault_not_enabled` search, daily schedule, rows and alerts; expected-Mac and exception lookup revisions; redacted MDM command/status responses with device ID, command/status ID, FileVault boolean, status time and collection time; collector/pagination health; fixtures; dashboard and case history; and a later authoritative enabled status or approved lifecycle change. This documentation-only review issued no MDM query, read no recovery key, and created no runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At dispatch 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z add active expected IDs `mac-fv-off`, `mac-fv-stale`, and `mac-fv-missing`. Index `mac-fv-off` at 11:00 with `filevault_enabled=false`; `mac-fv-stale` at 2026-07-28T11:59:59Z with true; and no 48-hour event for missing. Expect exactly three rows with `filevault_disabled`, `status_stale` age 86401, and `not_observed_in_48h`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Require zero rows for an expected Mac with true status exactly 86400 seconds old or newer; disabled/future/expired/non-macOS inventory; an ungoverned observed device; or a qualifying exact device ID with a future exception, reason, ticket, and owner. Expiry equal to dispatch does not suppress. A true FileVault value with unknown recovery-key escrow remains outside this rule.

dataSources: Preferred source: a device-management service's Apple `SecurityInfo` response (`FDE_Enabled`) or macOS 14+ declarative FileVault status, exported through its documented API/webhook with command/status time and collection metadata. Normalize to `_time`, `device_id`, `platform`, `filevault_enabled`, `status_time`, `response_status`, `tenant`, `collector_time`, `request_id`, and `collector_version`. `index=endpoint_posture`, `sourcetype=local:apple:security_status`, snake_case aliases, and lookup names are local conventions. Do not collect PRK/CMS/bypass values. A local `fdesetup isactive` collector may be a separately validated fallback, not silently mixed with MDM semantics.
app: Apple device management protocol plus the selected MDM vendor API are authoritative for remote fleet status. A deployment-owned collector and Splunk search app provide normalization, lookups, fixtures, search, dashboard, and runbook. No HashiCorp Vault relationship or Splunkbase add-on is asserted.
spl:
| inputlookup expected_macos_filevault.csv
| eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), monitor_from_epoch=tonumber(monitor_from_epoch), monitor_until_epoch=tonumber(monitor_until_epoch), expected_row=1
| where lower(trim(monitor_enabled))="true" AND platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0 AND monitor_from_epoch<=now() AND monitor_until_epoch>now()
| fields device_id expected_row device_name serial_number owner criticality runbook
| append [ search index=endpoint_posture sourcetype=local:apple:security_status earliest=-48h latest=now
    | eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), filevault_enabled=case(filevault_enabled=true() OR lower(trim(filevault_enabled))="true",1,filevault_enabled=false() OR lower(trim(filevault_enabled))="false",0,true(),null()), observed_row=1
    | where platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0
    | stats latest(_time) AS status_time latest(filevault_enabled) AS filevault_enabled latest(response_status) AS response_status latest(collector_time) AS collector_time latest(request_id) AS request_id by device_id ]
| stats max(expected_row) AS expected_row max(observed_row) AS observed_row values(device_name) AS device_name values(serial_number) AS serial_number values(owner) AS owner values(criticality) AS criticality values(runbook) AS runbook max(status_time) AS status_time max(filevault_enabled) AS filevault_enabled values(response_status) AS response_status max(collector_time) AS collector_time values(request_id) AS request_id by device_id
| where expected_row=1
| eval status_age_seconds=if(isnull(status_time),null(),now()-status_time), finding=case(isnull(observed_row),"not_observed_in_48h",isnull(filevault_enabled),"unknown_filevault_value",filevault_enabled=0,"filevault_disabled",status_age_seconds>86400,"status_stale",true(),"healthy")
| where finding!="healthy"
| lookup macos_filevault_exceptions.csv device_id OUTPUT exception_until_epoch exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval stale_threshold_seconds=86400, observation_window_hours=48, use_case_id="UC-1.3.2"
| table device_id device_name serial_number finding filevault_enabled status_time status_age_seconds response_status collector_time request_id owner criticality runbook stale_threshold_seconds observation_window_hours use_case_id
| sort 0 finding -status_age_seconds device_id
description: Runs daily and emits one row per active expected Mac when no normalized FileVault observation exists in 48 hours, the latest value is unknown or explicitly false, or an enabled value is strictly older than 24 hours. The grain is exact lowercased device-management ID and rows preserve status/collection evidence and ownership.
value: An expected Mac without current FileVault evidence may expose data after loss or theft and may indicate enrollment, query, or encryption failure. Inventory-first results identify the exact coverage gap while keeping encryption state separate from recovery-key escrow and regulatory assurance.
implementation: Export Apple SecurityInfo or declarative FileVault status from the selected MDM, preserve command and collection health, and normalize only non-secret fields. Govern exact expected device IDs and finite exceptions. Run the inventory-first search daily, alert on false/unknown/stale/absent state, and verify the MDM record and device lifecycle before remediation. Track PRK escrow, secure-token users, conversion progress, and collector freshness as separate controls.
visualization: Show collector/MDM query freshness, response failures, expected coverage, duplicates, and unknown values before compliance counts. Display findings by owner/model/site with exact device ID, status age, and lifecycle; trend enabled/disabled/unknown/absent states. Drill down to redacted MDM evidence, profile/escrow status, exception, incident, and recovery. Never display recovery keys or call FileVault-on alone compliant.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; no CIM dataset is asserted for Apple FileVault state, expected-device absence, or recovery-key separation.

knownFalsePositives:
A finding reflects the defined evidence gap, but an approved lifecycle can explain it.

1. **New enrollment awaiting logout/login** — Apple deferred enablement can wait for user interaction. Confirm enrollment/profile state, deferral policy, owner, deadline, and MDM status; escalate after the approved grace period.

2. **Encryption/decryption transition** — A status can change during conversion. Verify authoritative progress and change ticket; never infer completion from an old boolean.

3. **Repair, wipe, migration, or retirement** — The old device ID may remain expected. Reconcile serial, old/new enrollment IDs, asset lifecycle, and ticket before changing inventory.

4. **MDM query/collector failure** — Permission, pagination, command timeout, or API outage can create absent/stale rows. Check canaries, response status, request ID, object totals, and collector time before endpoint action.

**Suppression mechanism:** the SPL uses `lookup macos_filevault_exceptions.csv` by exact `device_id` and requires future expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. Expired, wildcard, fleet-wide, collector-failure, or missing-escrow exceptions do not suppress.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and source contract

Assign MDM, macOS, identity, asset, security/privacy, Splunk, help-desk, and change owners. Qualify the MDM API and supported macOS/Splunk releases; this review ran none. Grant the collector only device/security-status read access. Explicitly prohibit indexing personal recovery keys, encrypted CMS key material, activation-lock bypass values, credentials, or unrestricted response bodies.

Prefer Apple's SecurityInfo `FDE_Enabled` response or macOS 14+ declarative FileVault status. Preserve the vendor's command/status ID, device ID, status time, response state, tenant, pagination, HTTP outcome, collection time, and collector version. Normalize the boolean with fixtures; unknown/null must not become false or true. If using local `fdesetup isactive`, maintain a separate source contract: its documented zero/true active result differs from an MDM observation, and it must not overwrite remote command metadata.

Create `expected_macos_filevault.csv` with unique exact device ID, platform, enabled flag, lifecycle epochs, serial, owner, criticality, and runbook. Reconcile with MDM/asset enrollment and retirement. Create exact finite `macos_filevault_exceptions.csv`. Monitor collector success, pagination/object count, command errors, latest known canary, duplicate IDs, null booleans, and index delay separately.

## Search, tests, and operations

Save the sidecar SPL, run daily, and trigger once per device/finding. The expected lookup creates absence rows; the event branch keeps latest 48-hour status; strict age >86400 makes exactly 24 hours healthy. Route broad absent/stale bursts first to MDM/data owners. Include no recovery material in alerts.

Run fixed-time controls plus true/false/null/string booleans, age 86399/86400/86401, no event, duplicate/newer status, wrong platform, lifecycle boundaries, exception expiry, delayed collection, API pagination loss, re-enrollment ID change, deferred enablement, conversion, and MDM migration. Compare lab rows with the MDM console and a controlled Mac. Keep draft until owners accept versions, privacy, status semantics, freshness, inventory, fixtures, alert delivery, and response.

Triage in order: collector/query health and canary; exact identity/lifecycle; latest redacted MDM status; profile and deferred-enablement state; conversion progress; secure-token/bootstrap-token prerequisites; PRK escrow/rotation in the MDM's protected workflow; then user/device condition. Do not automatically enable/disable FileVault, rotate/expose a PRK, add/remove unlock users, change secure tokens, wipe, or re-enroll from an alert. Close only after a new authoritative enabled status and separate recovery-key/control validation. A true boolean clears only this rule; it does not clear escrow, user authorization, or compliance controls.
grandmaExplanation: We compare every expected Mac with its management service and flag machines where FileVault is off or the answer is missing or old. Recovery-key safety is checked separately.
